payload.claim: `test_saffron_batch_stack_plans_once_and_runs_that_order`'s readiness-passes case never asserts the `repo` or `out_dir` values `_batch` hands to `_stack_runner`: `_recording_run_task(spec, spec_sha, *, repo_id, handoff, **kwargs)` swallows `repo`, `ledger`, `out_dir`, `base` and `ceilings` into `**kwargs` and checks none of them. Swapping `repo=repo` and `out_dir=out_dir` at the call site (`saffron/cli.py:936-938`) so the stack path hands `run_task` the artifact directory as the repo and the repo path as the output directory would leave every assertion in this test green, because only `repo_id` and `handoff` are read back. In production this would point every stacked task's git operations at a non-repo directory, a defect the gates cannot see because `repo` and `out_dir` are both plain `Path` values to the type checker.
